thread:
sana: FYI saw a cluster-wide uptick in Xid 31 during the 02:00 embedder batch window on us-west2-a10-rack. GPU0 and GPU3 on node rack-a10-14 have rising ECC_Corrected counters. Not sure if this is pure hardware or workload-affinity thing.

jonah: hmm, saw that too in the nightly job logs. The failures line up with heavy shared-batching for the embedder job id job-enc-77.

gpu-monitor-bot: ALERT: 2035001234 - Xid31 spikes detected on node rack-a10-14 (gpu0,gpu3). Recent jobs: job-enc-77 (embedder), job-ctx-21 (chat), job-rerank-3. ECC_CORRECTED: gpu0=124 -> 190 in last 1h, gpu3=98 -> 165 in last 1h.

ameer: can you paste the microtrace for one of the failure windows? need kernel and pcie errors.

lin: quick query I ran: ```sql
SELECT time, gpu, xid, job, batch_size, kernel_name
FROM gpu_events
WHERE node = 'rack-a10-14' AND time BETWEEN '2026-03-16T02:00:00Z' AND '2026-03-16T03:00:00Z' AND xid = 31
ORDER BY time;
```

lin: result sample: 2026-03-16T02:03:12Z gpu0 xid=31 job=job-enc-77 batch_size=64 kernel=multi_head_attn_fp16
2026-03-16T02:05:41Z gpu3 xid=31 job=job-enc-77 batch_size=128 kernel=kv_cache_write

ops: @sana do we have rack-level temp or power anomalies? thermal throttling can push ECC up.

gpu-monitor-bot: METRICS: rack-a10-14 temps: avg_gpu=78C -> peaks 86C during 02:02-02:06. PCIe CRC errors: gpu3 +2 in same window. No node reboot.

jonah: thermal spike + CRC + Xid31 on KV write kernel suggests either marginal card or a transient fabric error under high memory bandwidth. Do we see same cards across other jobs?

sana: I crosschecked: gpu0/gpu3 only show Xid31 when job-enc-77 runs with shared-batch enabled. When we isolate job to single gpu per pod (affinity=exclusive) Xid count drops to baseline.

ameer: that smells like job-level batching + sustained high p2p/PCIe stress. Two mitigation paths: (1) soft-drain the two GPUs and reassign pods with strict GPU affinity to avoid co-scheduling, or (2) tweak batcher to limit shared-batching for embeddings on A10s when ECC > threshold.

lin: config prototype for soft-drain labeling: ```kubectl label node rack-a10-14 gpu0=soft-drain --overwrite
# scheduler will avoid packing new shared-batch pods on labeled GPUs
```

ops: prefer not to full-drain during peak. Soft-drain + scheduled reprovision test during low-traffic window. We should also run memtest on the two cards.

jonah: agree. Proposed immediate actions: 1) apply soft-drain label, 2) change embedder batcher policy for job-enc-77 to "no-shared-batching" for that tenant, 3) run vendor stress test and memtest, 4) monitor Xid/ECC for 24h. Anyone object? :thumbsup:

sana: +1. I'll own steps 1 & 2.

ameer: I'll schedule memtest and a controlled pcie stress test. If vendor confirms flaky card, we replace under warranty. If tests pass but Xid persists only under large shared batches, we should update batcher heuristics to prefer lower batch aggregation on A10s during certain telemetry signals.

lin: logging note: creating enrichment rule to attach job tags to Xid events for future triage: job_name, batch_size, kernel_name, batcher_mode. That will help correlate workload affinity automatically.

ops: timeline?

sana: soft-drain applied 2035001300, adjusted batcher policy deployed 2035001325. Monitoring now.

gpu-monitor-bot: UPDATE: 2035001350 - after soft-drain + policy change, Xid31 events on rack-a10-14 decreased by 82% in last 10m window. ECC_CORRECTED trending down.

jonah: good signal. keep memtest and vendor ticket queued. Also ticket to runtime team: consider adding a "batching-safety" knob that disables shared-batching when ECC_CORRECTED delta > 50 in last 30m.

ameer: filing vendor RMA if memtest fails. If passes, we'll keep heuristics permanent and revisit hardware replacement cadence.

sana: thanks everyone. Will post follow-up summary in incidents channel after 24h observation. :eyes:
